IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE SANJAY DWIVEDI  ON THE 11th OF MARCH, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 25252 of 2022  DEEPANKAR VISHWAS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Akshay Jha - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Alok Agnihotri - Government Advocate for the responden
ORDER This first application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in relation to FIR/Crime No.276/2019 registered at Police Station Omti, District Jabalpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 409, 406 and,
420/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. On earlier occasion the bail application was heard but the present applicant was absconder and bail application filed for grant of anticipatory bail before the trial Court since was rejected on the ground that the applicant is absconding despite the fact that other co-accused persons have been granted bail considering the settlement took place between the parties

, therefore, the matter was referred to the Division Bench so as decide whether the absconder is entitled to get the benefit of anticipatory bail or not, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12213 2 MCRC-25252-2022 Court vide order dated 27.02.2025 has decided the reference observing therein that even for absconder, the anticipatory bail is permissible.

4. The counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was the Manager in a company in which the complainant has invested some amount so as to get the profit in a share business but ultimately Deepankar Vishwas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131421649/
1 he suffered a loss and the amount invested by him could not be received back, therefore, he made complaint to the police.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the applicant is only a Manager in the company and nothing more.
He submits that the applicant was working for the company does not mean that the amount had gone with him and he had used the amount for his personal use.

He submits that when the other accused persons have been granted bail considering the settlement took place between the parties, then there was no reason for trial Court for rejecting the bail application of the present applicant only on the ground that the applicant was absconder.

He submits that since this Court has decided in reference that the absconder is also entitled to get the benefit of anticipatory bail,
therefore, the present bail application can be considered.
5.

On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the submissions made by the counsel for the applicant, read over the case diary and submitted that the present applicant can go before the trial Court with the order of reference case and can move a fresh application.
He has submitted that the other accused persons have been granted regular bail but not the anticipatory bail, therefore, the present application deserves to be rejected.

6. However, considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case-diary, especially the facts and circumstances NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12213 3 MCRC-25252-2022 of the case, I am inclined to grant interim protection to the present applicant for the reasons that the agreement between the parties had been taken note of by the trial Court and only on the ground of absconder, his bail application was rejected but that issue has already been decided in favour of the applicant, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
8. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE ac/-
